meta.firmware: fn-h89 branch h89-disk-fixes HEAD 7ab84ae64 (BUILD_RS232, -DPINMAP_H89); the card side, PPIChannel and the pin map, from fujinet-firmware PR #2232 (h89-remove-245, 8ff4f7968)
meta.fujinet_lib: fujinet-lib branch h89-setup-after-reset 7fc847b (PR #249; surveyed at 9e6d4dd, which still set DIR and /OE)
meta.scope: bus level + disk, clock, printer, modem, cpm devices. Fuji (0x70) and network (0x71-0x78) command sets are out of scope here.

framing: SLIP constants: SLIP_END=0xC0, SLIP_ESCAPE=0xDB, SLIP_ESC_END=0xDC, SLIP_ESC_ESC=0xDD (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.h:16-21)
Encoder (firmware replies): exactly one 0xC0, then the packet with 0xC0 -> DB DC and 0xDB -> DB DD, then one 0xC0 (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:97-124)

Receive: the service loop reads bytes until it sees 0xC0 or a read timeout; every non-0xC0 byte read before that is handed to the modem as raw data (rs232Modem::tx), even when the modem is disabled in config (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:99-109)

On 0xC0 the bus collects bytes until a second 0xC0 has been read; that span is the frame (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:337-366). A frame must therefore be exactly C0 <body> C0: a doubled leading C0 (C0 C0 <body> C0) produces an empty 2-byte frame that is rejected silently, the body bytes are then read as raw modem data, and the trailing C0 opens a bogus frame (derived from rs232.cpp:99-116 + 337-359 and FujiBusPacket.cpp:150-151)

Decoder starts at the first 0xC0 in the buffer, stops at the next 0xC0; a malformed escape (DB followed by anything but DC/DD) drops both bytes; a truncated escape ends decoding (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:55-95)

Header (6 bytes, little-endian length on both ESP32 and x86): device u8, command u8, length u16 = total unescaped packet length incl. header, checksum u8, first descriptor u8 (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:17-26)

Frame rejected if: encoded span < 8 bytes or does not start and end with 0xC0 (FujiBusPacket.cpp:150-153); decoded < 6 bytes (157-158); header length != decoded length (164-165); checksum mismatch (170-176); descriptor chain or fields run past the end (193-194, 212-213)
No maximum frame size on the firmware side (ByteBuffer grows); the u16 length field caps a valid packet at 65535 bytes (FujiBusPacket.cpp:164, 283)
Bytes after the fields are the payload (data); a frame with no trailing bytes has no payload at all (data() is empty optional) (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:221-226)

checksum.coverage: Computed over the whole unescaped packet (header + descriptors + fields + payload) with the checksum byte set to 0 (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:166-176 receive, 284-287 send). An identical end-around-carry helper rs232_checksum exists at fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:36-44. fujinet-lib computes the same sum in two passes with a seed (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:56-65, 88-91).

descriptors: Low 3 bits of a descriptor index two tables: fieldSize {0,1,1,1,1,2,2,4} and numFields {0,1,2,3,4,1,2,1}; i.e. 0=no fields, 1..4 = that many u8 fields, 5 = one u16, 6 = two u16, 7 = one u32 (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:28-35)

Bit 7 (0x80) = another descriptor byte follows. The first descriptor is header byte 5; extra descriptor bytes come immediately after the header, before any field bytes (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:186-198)
Fields for all descriptors follow in order, each little-endian (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:200-219, read_le 46-52)

Bits 3-6 of a descriptor are ignored by the parser (mask 0x07) (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:203). fujinet-lib's H89 fuji_bus_call puts its raw 'fields' argument in the header, so FUJI_FIELD_DATA (0x08) and FUJI_FIELD_REPLY (0x10) appear on the wire in bits 3/4 and are ignored (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:201; fujinet-lib/include/fujinet-bus-ezcall.h:7-18)

Serializer (firmware->host packets) groups consecutive same-size params, at most 4 bytes per descriptor (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:243-279). Firmware replies never carry params, so reply descriptor is always 0 (rs232.cpp:396)
params: param(n) returns _params.at(n).value as uint32 regardless of the field's wire size (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.h:75-77); devices never check the field width, so a u8, u16 or u32 field all work where a number is expected
paramCount() counts fields across all descriptors (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.h:79-81)

A missing field makes .at() throw std::out_of_range. ESP32 H89 build has C++ exceptions off (fn-h89/sdkconfig.fujinet-heathkit-h89:422) so it aborts (reboot); fujinet-pc terminates on the uncaught exception. Guarded: disk R/P/W (disk.cpp:385-388), disk STATUS (395-396), clock alt flag (rs232Clock.h:14-17), printer STATUS (printer.cpp:241). Unguarded: modem SET_DUMP, LISTEN, BAUDRATELOCK (2 fields), AUTOANSWER, STATUS (modem.cpp:1632, 1635, 1641, 1644, 1648)

transaction_get copies min(requested, payload remaining); it fails only if the frame has no payload at all, and succeeds without looking when 0 bytes are requested (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:66-82). A short payload is therefore accepted (device buffer keeps its prior/zeroed contents), extra payload bytes are ignored
replies: Reply = one packet from the addressed device: header device = the replying device's ID, command = FUJI_ACK 0x06 or FUJI_NAK 0x15, descriptor 0, then data (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:379-399)
Data is attached only when ack is true; a NAK never carries data, even when the handler supplied some (rs232.cpp:390-394)
transaction_success -> ACK, no data; transaction_error -> NAK; transaction_send(data,len,is_error) -> ACK+data or bare NAK (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:53-64, 84-89)
EXCEPTION: anything 'sent' by the modem device (0x50) bypasses framing: data is written raw to the port and ACK/NAK with no data writes nothing at all (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:381-386)

Exactly one reply per accepted frame except: bad frame (silence), printer disabled (silence, printer.cpp:226-229), modem disabled (silence, modem.cpp:1612-1615), modem ACK/NAK (no bytes), and ROM mount pushes (extra unsolicited frames to device 0xFF before the Fuji reply, disk.cpp:28-110)

transaction_success asserts the state is NO_GET/DID_GET (rs232.cpp:55); assertions are enabled on the ESP32 H89 build (sdkconfig.fujinet-heathkit-h89:414), so a success after an error aborts (see modem LISTEN 0)
errors: Bad checksum, bad length, short/garbled frame: readBusPacket returns nullptr, 'packet fail' is logged and NOTHING is sent (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:111-116)

Read timeout inside a frame (gap longer than the channel read timeout): frame is incomplete, parse fails, silence (rs232.cpp:355-359, 365). The bytes that arrive after the gap are then read as raw modem data until the next C0 (rs232.cpp:99-107)

Unregistered device ID: _activeDev is nullptr, transaction_error() -> sendReplyPacket(_activeDev->id(), false) -> fujiIDForDevice(nullptr) -> value_or(0), so the NAK header carries device 0x00 (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:126-133, 60-64, 401-404; fn-h89/lib/bus/bus.h:50-52). Calls a member on nullptr (works because id() is non-virtual)
The bus does not consult device_active / enable state before dispatch (rs232.cpp:126-128); each device decides
No RESEND/retry command or retransmission exists anywhere in lib/bus/rs232 or PPIChannel (grep: none)

fujinet-lib accepts a reply only if rlen >= 6, rlen == header.length, checksum matches, device == request device and command == 0x06; any NAK, device-00 NAK or timeout returns false (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:108-164)
timeouts: ESP32 H89 (PPIChannel): inter-byte receive timeout = IOCHANNEL_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT 100 ms; PPIChannel::begin() never changes read_timeout_ms (fn-h89/lib/hardware/IOChannel.h:4, 40; fn-h89/lib/hardware/PPIChannel.cpp:32-66). The timer restarts on every byte received (fn-h89/lib/hardware/IOChannel.cpp:24-38)

ESP32 H89 transmit: per byte, waits for IBF low; gives up after 1 s (PPI_TX_TIMEOUT_US 1000000) and returns the count sent so far; busy-polls 2 ms then yields with vTaskDelay(1) (fujinet-firmware PR #2232, lib/hardware/PPIChannel.cpp:14-15, 150-169). Also aborts immediately if /OBF goes low (host started sending) - 'reply cut short' (152-158). /STB held until IBF rises or 100 us, then the data held 1 us more (16-17, 171-184)

fujinet-pc: TTYChannel opened with readTimeout(200) ms (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:229-241; UARTChannel=TTYChannel on Unix fn-h89/lib/hardware/UARTChannel.h:8-9); BoIP channel keeps its 500 ms default (fn-h89/lib/hardware/BoIPChannel.h:8, 27; rs232.cpp:216-224)

fujinet-lib H89: reply wait TIMEOUT_SLOW = 15*PORT_TICKS_PER_SECOND = 7500 ticks of 2 ms = 15 s, applied per byte (resets on each byte) (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:14, 106-107; fujinet-lib/bus/h89/portio.h:4; fujinet-lib/bus/h89/portio.c:142-158). Tick counter TIKCNT 0x000B under CP/M, 0x201B under HDOS (portio.c:52-57)
fujinet-lib H89 port_putc has NO timeout: two unbounded busy-waits on /OBF (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/portio.c:160-173). If the ESP32 is not taking bytes the H89 hangs
ppi_channel: Selected when ESP_PLATFORM && PIN_PPI_OBF: FUJINET_OVER_PPI, _serial is a PPIChannel (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.h:23-25, 134-135); PINMAP_H89 defines the pins (fn-h89/include/pinmap/heathkit_h89.h:29-43). fujinet-pc never builds PPIChannel (pinmap only included under ESP_PLATFORM, fn-h89/lib/hardware/PPIChannel.h:4-8) and uses TTY or BoIP

Hardware: 82C55 in Mode 2 at H89 port 0xD0, port A wired straight to ESP32 D0-D7 = GPIO 32,33,25,26,27,14,12,13 (the 74LVC245 that was between them is gone, PR #2232); ESP32 outputs /STB (GPIO4 -> PC4) and /ACK (GPIO15 -> PC6); inputs IBF (GPIO34 <- PC5), /OBF (GPIO35 <- PC7) (fujinet-firmware PR #2232, include/pinmap/heathkit_h89.h:28-40). Before it, PR #2042 (7e8e647) read the 245's DIR on GPIO22 <- PC0 and /OE on GPIO21 <- PC1, and earlier firmware GPIO2 and GPIO0 (fn-h89/include/pinmap/heathkit_h89.h:4-7, 29-43). The reworked card leaves the ESP32's EN, IO0 and IO2 unconnected

H89->ESP32: while /OBF is low the ESP32, in a critical section, pulls /ACK low, which makes the 82C55 drive port A, waits 1 us, samples D0-D7, raises /ACK, and appends the byte to the FIFO (fujinet-firmware PR #2232, lib/hardware/PPIChannel.cpp:123-139). The firmware before #2232 first checked DIR=1 and /OE=0

ESP32->H89: per byte wait for IBF=0; drive D0-D7, pulse /STB low until IBF rises (max 100 us), hold the data 1 us, release the data lines (fujinet-firmware PR #2232, lib/hardware/PPIChannel.cpp:141-187). Data pins are only driven during a strobe (75-79, 81-95). The firmware before #2232 also waited for DIR=0 and /OE=0

No baud rate (getBaudrate 0, setBaudrate no-op) and no modem-control lines: getDTR/getRTS true, setRI/setDSR/setCTS/setDCD no-ops (fn-h89/lib/hardware/PPIChannel.h:38-49). So the network 'data pending' interrupt that rs232.cpp drives with setRI (rs232.cpp:186-187) never reaches the H89
Input flush at bus setup is skipped for the PPI (the 8255 holds a request sent during boot) (fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:266-271)

H89 side (fujinet-lib): port C bit map PC2 ESP32 EN (not connected on the reworked card, #2042), PC3 INTR, PC4 /STB, PC5 IBF, PC6 /ACK, PC7 /OBF; PC0 and PC1 (the 245's DIR and /OE once) are no longer named (fujinet-lib 7fc847b, bus/h89/portio.c:14-19). port_init writes the mode word C2H (port A Mode 2, port B an input) and reads port A, every time (42-50). port_putc waits /OBF high and OUTs port A (95-102). port_getc reads port A when IBF is set (52-60)

commands.name: DISK_READ

fields.name: sector
fields.meaning: 0-based sector number; byte offset = sector*512 on IMG (fn-h89/lib/media/rs232/diskTypeImg.cpp:17-20), IMD LBA = sector (fn-h89/lib/media/rs232/diskTypeIMD.cpp:12-18)

reply.len: IMG: 512; IMD: that sector's native size (128..512); ROM: never succeeds
naks_when: no image ever mounted or unmounted (device_active false) (disk.cpp:125-130)
IMG: sector >= image_size/512 or file handle closed (diskTypeImg.cpp:31-35)
IMD: sector >= LBA count or record unreadable (diskTypeIMD.cpp:153-171)

commands.side_effects: IMD: sets controller status bits (CRC error 0x08, deleted 0x20, missing 0x10) visible in the next DISK_STATUS byte 1 (diskTypeIMD.cpp:176-183)
traps: Sector numbers are 0-based although diskTypeImg.cpp:16 says '1-based' (diskTypeImg.cpp:17-20)
A trailing partial 512-byte block of an IMG is unreachable: sector count = size/512 truncated (diskTypeImg.cpp:162)
An IMD sector with a data error or deleted mark is still returned with ACK; only DISK_STATUS shows it (diskTypeIMD.cpp:173-183)

fujinet_lib.symbol: none (no disk API); use DEVCALL_C1234_RV(0x31+n, DISKCMD_READ, sector, buf, 512)
fujinet_lib.sends: descriptor 0x17 (7|REPLY) + u32 LE sector, no payload
fujinet_lib.mismatch: fuji_bus_call returns only true/false: an IMD reply shorter than the buffer still succeeds and the caller cannot learn the length (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:108)

commands.name: DISK_WRITE

payload.format: sector data; shorter payload is zero-padded (buffer memset to 0 first, disk.cpp:151-153), longer is truncated

naks_when: IMG: sector >= size/512 (diskTypeImg.cpp:69-73) - fixed in 7ab84ae64, previously grew the file
IMG mounted read-only (file opened "rb", fwrite short) (fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.cpp:596-598; diskTypeImg.cpp:92-97)
IMD mounted read-only, out of range, unavailable sector, or record cannot take the data (diskTypeIMD.cpp:196-227)

commands.side_effects: IMG writes 512 bytes at sector*512 and fflush()es (diskTypeImg.cpp:82-104); IMD writes in place and flushes (diskTypeIMD.cpp:220-230)
traps: verify flag (WRITE vs PUT) is ignored by every media type (diskTypeImg.cpp:63-105; diskTypeIMD.cpp:193)
IMD out-of-range sector: sector_size()=0 -> zero-length get succeeds -> write() NAKs (diskTypeIMD.cpp:245-250; rs232.cpp:71-72)

commands.name: DISK_PUT
traps: Identical to DISK_WRITE; the only difference (verify=false, disk.cpp:392) is ignored downstream

commands.name: DISK_STATUS

layout: byte0 drive status: 0x80 'enhanced' if PERCOM spt==26 (IMG) / _spt==26 (IMD); 0x40 double-sided if PERCOM num_sides==1 (IMG) / heads>1 (IMD); 0x20 double density if sector size >128 (IMG: never, see traps) / MFM (IMD); 0x08 write-protect (IMD read-only only)
byte1 = ~controller status (0xFF = clear; IMD clears bits 0x40 WP, 0x20 deleted, 0x10 missing, 0x08 CRC, 0x04 data lost after an error)

traps: Answers even with nothing mounted: 00 FF E0 00 (disk.cpp:206-217)

IMG never reports double density: _disk_sector_size stays at its 128 default (diskType.h:57) because MediaTypeImg::mount never sets it (diskTypeImg.cpp:157-166, 111-112). Normal IMG reply: 00 FF E0 00
ROM media: 00 00 00 00 (diskTypeROM.cpp:48-51)
After unmount the stale media object still answers (disk.cpp:212-213)
Was mapped onto WRITE before 7ab84ae64 (commit message); fixed at HEAD (disk.cpp:394-397)
commands.notes: Atari 810/XF551 status layout documented in comments disk.cpp:172-200

commands.name: DISK_FORMAT

layout: IMG: FF FF then 126 x 00 (an empty Atari bad-sector list)

commands.side_effects: NONE on IMG - the image file is not touched (diskTypeImg.cpp:130-142)
traps: FORMAT does not format: IMG just ACKs (diskTypeImg.cpp:130-142)
Reply length is _disk_sector_size = 128, not 512 (diskTypeImg.cpp:139; diskType.h:57)
No device_active check: after unmount an IMG drive still ACKs (disk.cpp:226)

commands.name: DISK_FORMAT_MEDIUM
traps: Alias of DISK_FORMAT

IMD: filled at mount: tracks=max cyl+1, step 1, spt=max, sides=heads-1, density, sector_size=largest sector, drive_present 0xFF (diskTypeIMD.cpp:66-77)

image_types: Type is chosen by filename extension only (fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/disk.cpp:299-300; fn-h89/lib/media/rs232/diskType.cpp:59-96)

.IMD (case-insensitive) -> MediaTypeIMD: native geometry, per-sector sizes 128..512, read-only unless the slot is mounted for write; images with sectors > 512 bytes or no sectors are refused (fn-h89/lib/media/IMDImage.cpp:151-157; fn-h89/lib/media/rs232/diskTypeIMD.cpp:79-134; disk.cpp:317-327)

.ROM .BIN .INT .ITV .CHF .NES .SMS .A78 .A52 .ST2 -> MediaTypeROM: whole file pushed at mount time to DBC device 0xFF as NET_OPEN/NET_WRITE/NET_CLOSE frames sent by the firmware, each awaiting an ACK; R/W/FORMAT always NAK (diskType.cpp:86-93; disk.cpp:28-110, 305-316; diskTypeROM.cpp:31-46)

.XEX and every other extension (or none) -> MediaTypeImg: flat file of 512-byte sectors, sector n at byte n*512, count = size/512 (diskType.cpp:69-72, 95; disk.cpp:328-334; diskTypeImg.cpp:17-20, 157-166)
extra.sector_size: Fixed 512 for IMG and the MediaType default (diskType.cpp:19-22); IMD = that sector's real size (diskTypeIMD.cpp:247-250). Sector buffer is 512 bytes (diskType.h:12)
extra.rom_mount_trap: On the H89 the ROM push frames (device 0xFF, NET_OPEN 0x4F with 5-byte payload id+u32 size) are written to the H89 while it waits for the MOUNT_IMAGE reply; nothing answers them, readBusPacket gets nothing within the read timeout, the push fails, mount returns MEDIATYPE_UNKNOWN and MOUNT_IMAGE NAKs (disk.cpp:44-51; rs232.h:178-186; rs232.cpp:337-366; fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.cpp:631). fujinet-lib sees the 0xFF frame first and fails on device mismatch (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:149-156); the later NAK frame is left for the next call. Any H89 file named *.BIN is caught by this
extra.mount_failure: mount() returning MEDIATYPE_UNKNOWN makes MOUNT_IMAGE NAK (fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.cpp:625-632)
extra.unmount: unmount() closes the file and clears device_active but keeps the media object; READ/WRITE check device_active, STATUS/FORMAT/PERCOM do not (disk.cpp:125-130, 147, 355-365)

commands.name: PRINTER_WRITE

payload.format: raw bytes to the printer emulator

naks_when: emulator could not open/append the output file (printer.cpp:48-51; fn-h89/lib/printer-emulator/printer_emulator.cpp:70-80)

commands.side_effects: Bytes go through the selected emulator into file "/paper" on the SD card if mounted, else flash (fn-h89/lib/printer-emulator/printer_emulator.cpp:7, 83-89; fn-h89/src/main.cpp:353). Retrieved via the web UI GET /print, which closes the output (fn-h89/lib/http/httpService.cpp:2207 ESP32; fn-h89/lib/http/mgHttpService.cpp:1715 fujinet-pc). The first print after that truncates and restarts the file (printer_emulator.cpp:74-80, 133-146)
traps: Buffer overrun: memcpy(provideBuffer(), data, len) with no bound into uint8_t buffer[320] - payloads > 320 bytes overwrite the emulator object (printer.cpp:46; fn-h89/lib/printer-emulator/printer_emulator.h:41, 72)
Length truncated to 8 bits: process(uint8_t linelen, ...) gets len mod 256, so 256 bytes print nothing (still ACK) and 300 bytes print the first 44 (printer.cpp:48; printer_emulator.h:68)

Default type FILE_TRIM writes up to and including the first 0x9B (ATASCII EOL) and drops the rest of the record (fn-h89/lib/printer-emulator/file_printer.cpp:20-27; fn-h89/include/atascii.h:12). setEOL('\r') does not affect the file printer
FILE_ASCII drops CR and LF (keeps only 32..122 except 96, after &0x7F) so lines run together on the H89 (file_printer.cpp:28-58)
Printer disabled in config -> no reply at all (silence), not a NAK (printer.cpp:226-229); default enabled (fn-h89/lib/config/fnConfig.h:487)
commands.pc_vs_esp32: ESP32: SD or SPIFFS flash; fujinet-pc: the SD directory (default "SD", fn-h89/lib/config/fnConfig.h:30)

commands.name: PRINTER_PUT
traps: Alias of PRINTER_WRITE

commands.name: PRINTER_STATUS

fields.name: reqType
fields.meaning: value ignored but the field MUST be present

traps: Byte 1 is an uninitialized member (printer.h:27; printer.cpp:96; object created with new at main.cpp:360)

not_dispatched: Any other command -> NAK (printer.cpp:252-253); disabled printer -> silence for every command (printer.cpp:226-229)

extra.printer_types: Selected from config printer slot 0, PRINTER_INVALID -> PRINTER_FILE_TRIM (fn-h89/src/main.cpp:354-356). Types: 0 file RAW, 1 file TRIM, 2 file ASCII, 3 Atari 820, 4 822, 5 825, 6 1020, 7 1025, 8 1027, 9 1029, 10 XMM801, 11 XDM121, 12 Epson 80, 13 Epson PrintShop, 14 Okimate 10, 15 GRANTIC (PNG), 16 HTML, 17 HTML ATASCII (fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/printer.h:32-76; printer.cpp:103-177)
extra.emulator_setup: Every type gets setEOL('\r') and setTranslate850(true) (printer.cpp:174-175)
extra.raw_mode: PRINTER_FILE_RAW writes all n bytes unmodified (file_printer.cpp:15-18) - the only mode that is byte-transparent for H89 text

commands.name: MODEM_CONTROL

fields.meaning: ignored (DTR/RTS/XMT code is under #ifdef OBSOLETE, modem.cpp:183-215)

layout: nothing is written (modem ACK is raw with no data, rs232.cpp:381-386)

traps: No reply bytes at all

fujinet_lib.mismatch: any fuji_bus_call to 0x50 waits for a frame that never comes: false after the 15 s timeout (fuji_bus_call.c:106-116)

commands.name: MODEM_CONFIGURE

fields.meaning: ignored; baud code hard-wired to SIO_BAUD_9600 (modem.cpp:250-256)

commands.side_effects: modemBaud = 9600 unless baud-locked (modem.cpp:258-292); affects CONNECT text and the next MODEM_STREAM
traps: Always 9600 regardless of the request

commands.name: MODEM_SET_DUMP

fields.name: enable
fields.meaning: nonzero enables the modem sniffer (traffic capture file)

traps: Missing field aborts the firmware

commands.name: MODEM_LISTEN

fields.name: port
fields.meaning: TCP listen port (truncated to unsigned short)

commands.side_effects: Stops client and server, then tcpServer.begin(port) with max 1 client; incoming calls then produce RING (or auto-answer) (modem.cpp:365-380, 1327-1345)
traps: port 0: transaction_error() then transaction_success() -> assert(state) fails -> abort on the ESP32 (assertions on) (modem.cpp:372-380; rs232.cpp:55; sdkconfig.fujinet-heathkit-h89:414)

commands.name: MODEM_UNLISTEN
commands.side_effects: tcpClient.stop(); tcpServer.stop() - also drops an active call

commands.name: MODEM_BAUDRATELOCK
traps: Two fields required

commands.name: MODEM_STATUS

layout: 1 = 0xC0 if connected or a caller is waiting, + 0x0C same condition, + 0x01 if TCP data available or caller waiting: so 0x00, 0xCC or 0xCD

commands.side_effects: If auto-answer is on and a caller waits: modemActive=true, answerTimer started (modem.cpp:154-159)
traps: Reply is 2 raw bytes, NOT a SLIP frame (rs232.cpp:381-386)

fujinet_lib.mismatch: fuji_bus_call discards bytes until 0xC0, so it skips these 2 bytes and times out (port_slip.c:56-61)

commands.name: MODEM_WRITE

payload.format: command mode: one AT command line (whole payload); online: raw bytes for the TCP peer

layout: no ACK bytes; any AT result text is raw and mostly suppressed (see traps)

commands.side_effects: Command mode: payload becomes cmd and modemCommand() runs (exact "ATA\r" instead sets answerHack, answered on the next service pass) (modem.cpp:103-114, 1317-1324). Online: tcpClient.write(payload) with no telnet escaping and no sniffer (modem.cpp:115-119)
traps: cmdOutput is forced false for the whole command (modem.cpp:105, 113) and every at_cmd_println() returns early when it is false (modem.cpp:468, 484, 504, 525): OK/ERROR/help/IP/echo text is never sent for commands given this way
Numeric results (ATV0) still emit CR LF but the digits go to an unsent _packetData buffer (modem.cpp:456-461, 1665-1683)
No payload -> returns without action (modem.cpp:100-101)

commands.name: MODEM_STREAM

layout: Atari POKEY AUDF/AUDC values for modemBaud: default 28 A0 00 A0 28 A0 00 A0 78 (19200 / unknown baud); bytes 0,4 and 2,6 vary per baud (modem.cpp:315-351)

traps: fujinet-pc on a TTY: the HOST LINK baud changes to modemBaud (e.g. 9600 after MODEM_CONFIGURE) (rs232.cpp:323-335); PPI: setBaudrate is a no-op (PPIChannel.h:39); BoIP: skipped (rs232.cpp:333)
Raw 9-byte reply, not a frame

not_dispatched: MODEM_READ 0x52, MODEM_TYPE3_POLL 0x40, MODEM_TYPE1_POLL 0x3F, MODEM_LOAD_HANDLER 0x26, MODEM_LOAD_RELOCATOR 0x21 and anything else -> transaction_error -> modem raw path with no data -> NOTHING sent (modem.cpp:1659-1660; rs232.cpp:381-386)
Modem disabled in config -> silence for every command (modem.cpp:1612-1615); default enabled (fnConfig.h:534)

data_flow_h89_to_modem: Raw bytes sent outside any frame (anything before a 0xC0) go to rs232Modem::tx -> rs232_write, exactly like a MODEM_WRITE payload (rs232.cpp:99-109; modem.cpp:1574-1577). Chunks end at the channel read timeout (100 ms PPI / 200 ms TTY / 500 ms BoIP) or at a 0xC0, so a slowly typed AT command arrives as several separate 'commands' (derived)
This path runs even when the modem is disabled in config (rs232.cpp:106-107)
data_flow_modem_to_h89: All modem output is unframed raw bytes via rx() -> sendReplyPacket(0x50) -> _port->write (modem.cpp:1579-1598; rs232.cpp:381-386)

Emitted only in service passes with no host input pending (rs232.cpp:162-170): TCP data (modem.cpp:1498-1516, telnet-decoded if ATNET1), RING every 3 s (1327-1345, RING_INTERVAL modem.h:63), 'CONNECT <baud>' ~1 s after a dial/answer (1427-1440, ANSWER_TIMER_MS modem.h:67), 'NO CARRIER' on disconnect (1536-1571)

The H89 must poll the 8255 and separate these bytes from frames itself; fujinet-lib has no modem API (port_getc_timeout is exported, fujinet-lib/bus/h89/portio.h:9). fujinet-lib's frame reader discards non-C0 bytes before a reply (port_slip.c:56-61), so stray modem bytes before a reply are lost, and a 0xC0 inside modem data would desynchronise it

PPI: each rx() call blocks the single firmware service loop up to 1 s per byte while the H89 is not reading, then drops the rest (PPIChannel.cpp:157-176); at_cmd_println emits CR and LF as separate rx() calls (modem.cpp:477-480)
at_commands: Matched by prefix, in table order, against an upper-cased, whitespace-trimmed copy; 0x9B is turned into CR; plain 'AT' must match exactly (modem.cpp:1031-1064). Table (modem.cpp:983-1029):
ATNET0 / ATNET1 -> telnet processing off/on for received data (1120-1133); default off (modem.h:174)
ATA -> answer a waiting caller (1134-1136, 793-808)
ATIP -> prints IP or 'WiFi is not connected.' (1138-1147)
ATH, +++ATH, ATH2 (AT_OFFHOOK) -> hang up: NO CARRIER if connected else OK (1075-1106)
ATDT<host>[:port], ATDP, ATDI -> TCP connect, port default 23; all-digit host looked up in the phonebook; host 5551234 fakes a CONNECT for BobTerm (1108-1112, 810-881)
ATWIFILIST -> scan and list (1113-1115, 743-791)
ATWIFICONNECT<ssid>,<key> -> join WiFi, blocks up to 20 s (1116-1118, 543-596)
ATGET<url> -> TCP connect + HTTP/1.1 GET, then online (1151-1153, 627-691)
ATPORT<n> -> set listen port and start server (1154-1156, 598-625)
ATV0 / ATV1 -> numeric / verbose results (1157-1164)
ATS0=0 / ATS0=1 -> auto-answer off/on (1165-1178)
ATE0 / ATE1 -> echo off/on (1179-1192)
Ignored, answer OK: AT&F, ATS2=43, ATS5=8, ATS6=2, ATS7=30, ATS12=20, ATM0, ATM1, ATX1, AT&C1, AT&D2, AT&W, +++ATZ, 'ATS2=128 X1 M0' (1193-1211)
AT+SNIFF / AT-SNIFF -> modem sniffer on/off (1212-1225)
AT+TERM=VT52, AT+TERM=VT100, AT+TERM=ANSI, AT+TERM=DUMB -> telnet TTYPE (1226-1253)
ATCPM -> CRASH: SYSTEM_BUS.getCPM() is nullptr on this build (1254-1258; rs232.h:159)
ATPBLIST / ATPBCLEAR / ATPB<num>=<host>[:port] (ATPB<num> deletes) -> phonebook (1259-1271, 884-972)
ATO -> back online if still connected (1272-1297)
anything else -> ERROR (1298-1303)
at_traps: Help text names commands that do not exist: ATPHONEBOOKLIST, ATPHONEBOOKCLR, AT[UN]SNIFF, ATTERMVT52/VT100/DUMB/ANSI (modem.h:29-36) - real spellings are ATPBLIST, ATPBCLEAR, AT+SNIFF/AT-SNIFF, AT+TERM=...
AT+TERM=ANSI sets DUMB and AT+TERM=DUMB sets ANSI: table strings (modem.cpp:1023-1024) are in a different order from the enum (modem.h:130-131)

+++ escape is dead: plusCount is only incremented inside #ifdef OBSOLETE (modem.cpp:1442-1491), so the check at 1521-1533 never fires. Online, MODEM_WRITE and raw bytes go straight to TCP (modem.cpp:115-119), so the H89 cannot send ATH; the call ends only when the peer disconnects or the H89 sends MODEM_UNLISTEN (modem.cpp:386-392, 1536-1571)
ATWIFICONNECT parsing is off: with a comma the SSID keeps the comma (substr(13, keyIndex-13+1)); without one it starts at offset 6 ('CONNECT...') (modem.cpp:549, 556)
ATGET host includes the ':' or '/' that ends it (substr(12, portIndex-12+1)), so only a bare 'ATGEThttp://host' works (modem.cpp:650)
Non-numeric port in ATDT/ATPORT/ATGET -> std::stoi throws -> abort (modem.cpp:601, 647, 861)

at_cmd_println(std::string) appends to _packetData which is never sent, so string output (e.g. ATIP address, ATPBLIST entries, dial echo of host) is lost even when output is enabled (modem.cpp:523-541, 1679-1683)
Result text of AT commands is suppressed in both input paths (cmdOutput=false in rs232_write, modem.cpp:103-114); only asynchronous RING/CONNECT/NO CARRIER and TCP data reach the H89
extra.listen_port_feature: MODEM_LISTEN(port) or ATPORT<n> starts a 1-client TCP server; with auto-answer off the modem prints RING every 3 s in command mode until ATA ('ATA\r' as a MODEM_WRITE payload is special-cased); with auto-answer on it answers itself; a second caller while online is sent a busy message and dropped (modem.cpp:363-381, 598-625, 1327-1345, 1419-1424)
extra.baud: modemBaud starts at SYSTEM_BUS.getBaudrate() = 115200 (modem.cpp:75; rs232.h:19, 128) and is only reported in CONNECT text / STREAM reply

commands.name: CPM_INIT

layout: On this build: NAK with device 0x00 (unregistered)
naks_when: always on the H89 build (rs232.cpp:126-133; main.cpp:346-366)

commands.side_effects: Would: ACK, wait 5 s, malloc 64 KB, set cpmActive; the service loop then gives the whole port to RunCPM's internal CCP until BIOS 0 (rs232cpm.cpp:27-75, 81-87; rs232.cpp:156-160)
traps: Not registered, and ATCPM dereferences the null CPM pointer (modem.cpp:1256-1257)

not_dispatched: CPM_WRITE 0x57, CPM_STATUS 0x53, CPM_READ 0x52, CPM_BOOT 0x42 -> would NAK (rs232cpm.cpp:88-90); on this build every 0x5A frame gets NAK device 0x00

extra.instance: rs232CPM sioZ exists (fn-h89/lib/device/device.h:49) but is never added to the bus

open_questions: fujinet-pc build type for the H89 target: whether NDEBUG is set (assert in transaction_success, rs232.cpp:55) - decides whether MODEM_LISTEN 0 aborts on PC too
Which transport the H89 emulator uses to reach fujinet-pc (TTY pty at Config baud vs BoIP) - sets the inter-byte timeout to 200 ms or 500 ms
The ROM-mount desync (unsolicited 0xFF frames, late NAK) is derived from code, not observed on hardware or emulator
Modem output suppression (cmdOutput=false during every AT command) looks like an RS232 port regression; confirm on hardware that 'AT' produces no 'OK'
Printer STATUS byte 1 value in practice (uninitialized member)
Whether real H89 programs ever send a frame with gaps > 100 ms (e.g. from interpreted BASIC); if so the remainder becomes raw modem input
